meta_hash_note: The whole-file SHA-256 changes after cleaning, because the metadata bytes change. The decoded-content SHA-256 must stay the same: those are the pixels or the audio samples, and they are compared before anything is saved.

meta_limits: The inspector reads the file locally. A content credential is reported, but its signature is not validated: the trust list and the certificate chain are not part of PHANTOM. Attribution fields are offered unticked — removing an author's name is your decision. A missing manifest does not prove that the file carries no other traces.

meta_provenance_none: Content credentials: no manifest found. PHANTOM does not verify authenticity; a missing manifest proves nothing about the rest of the file.
meta_provenance_unverified: Content credentials: manifest found, signature not verified — authenticity is not confirmed.

settings_threat_model:
Protects: the content of hidden data (AES-256-GCM). Where every bit of the carrier sits — the sealed header included — is derived from your password, so without it there is no region to read: a wrong password is indistinguishable from a carrier with no payload.
Does NOT protect: the presence of steganography itself — LSB embedding is detectable by statistical steganalysis; file metadata; re-compression of image or audio.
In messengers send the file AS A DOCUMENT: the “photo” mode re-encodes images and destroys the payload.
settings_wipe_warning: Overwriting a file cannot guarantee erasure on SSDs, copy-on-write filesystems (APFS/Btrfs) or journals. Treat it as risk reduction, not a guarantee.
